strengths.title: AI call telemetry schema anticipates real needs
strengths.preserve: Keep per-surface latency/success capture when wiring usage quotas and cost attribution; the table design is already right.

strengths.title: Build plan anchored modules to specs tightly enough that drift is detectable
strengths.preserve: Keep plans anchored to named sections so future audits can diff intent against implementation mechanically.

strengths.preserve: Keep CLAUDE.md-style files as pure redirects when adding new agent tools so memory has exactly one source per scope.

strengths.preserve: Never introduce synonyms (purchase/spending/outlay) into the finance domain; the one-noun discipline is what keeps both backends greppable.

findings.title: AI-generated output is executed with new Function and injected as raw SVG in the renderer
findings.impact: Any content that steers the explainer model (a crafted topic, OCR text from an uploaded image, or a compromised/malicious free-tier model) can make the browser execute arbitrary JavaScript in the logged-in session via the function-graph block, or inject script-bearing SVG. The payload persists in ConceptExplanation.explanationText and re-executes on every future render of that explanation.
findings.fix: Remove the new Function sink: parse equations with a restricted math parser (mathjs evaluate with a narrow node allowlist, or a small shunting-yard evaluator) and render plots from its output. Sanitize every AI-derived HTML/SVG sink with DOMPurify (allowing only svg/path/circle/etc.) before dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and strip event handlers and foreignObject.
findings.verify: rg -n "new Function" frontend/components && rg -c "DOMPurify.sanitize" frontend/components (expect 0 and >=2)

findings.title: No rate limiting or brute-force throttling exists on any endpoint including passcode verification
findings.impact: The internet-facing Render URL accepts unlimited guesses against the single shared APP_PASSCODE that guards every endpoint, and unlimited invocations of paid AI endpoints once any caller holds the passcode. A leaked passcode cannot be contained by lockout because no counter exists.
findings.fix: Add express-rate-limit (and a Vercel edge rate limit on the relay): strict window on /api/auth*, per-key windows on AI and export endpoints, and a failure counter with temporary lockout mirroring the journal-unlock brake already present in frontend/lib/session.ts.
findings.verify: rg -n "rateLimit" backend/src/server.ts frontend/app/api/auth/route.ts (expect >=2 sites)

findings.title: AI credential encryption has no rotation path and falls back to SESSION_SECRET
findings.impact: Rotating SESSION_SECRET (the documented session-signing secret) silently breaks decryption of every stored provider API key, taking AI features down until keys are re-entered; there is no versioned key id to perform a controlled re-encryption rotation after suspected compromise.
findings.fix: Add keyVersion column to AiProviderCredential, derive keys via HKDF with a recorded key id, require AI_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY explicitly (drop the SESSION_SECRET fallback), and add a re-encrypt-on-boot routine that migrates rows from old key versions.
findings.verify: rg -n "SESSION_SECRET" backend/src/lib/ai/credentials.ts (expect 0) && rg -n "keyVersion" backend/prisma/schema.prisma

findings.title: Sensitive-data protection is inconsistent across stores and AI logs retain full prompt text
findings.impact: Personal study notes and topics sit plaintext in Cloudflare D1 while journals get encryption, so the privacy guarantee documented for the journal does not extend to sibling personal data; unbounded prompt/response previews grow AiCallLog rows forever and embed user content (topics, notes, names) in Postgres with no retention or truncation policy.
findings.fix: Encrypt tracker payloads with the same door-journal AES-GCM envelope (or document why tracker data is lower-class), truncate promptPreview/responsePreview to ~500 chars at write time, and add a retention prune (e.g. delete AiCallLog rows older than 30 days) to the cron tick.
findings.verify: rg -n "door-journal:v1:" backend/src/lib/private-tracker-store.ts (expect >=1) && rg -n "slice\(0, 500\)" backend/src/server.ts near aiCallLog writes

findings.title: No secret scanning is wired into pre-commit or CI
findings.impact: A future commit carrying a provider key (the repo keeps live .env files locally beside the working tree) would reach GitHub unnoticed; nothing fails the build on credential shapes.
findings.fix: Add gitleaks to a pre-commit hook and as a hard-gating CI step over full history (--no-banner, no continue-on-error).
findings.verify: grep -c gitleaks .github/workflows/*.yml .pre-commit-config.yaml

findings.title: API responses ship without security headers and internal error messages reach clients
findings.impact: Prisma/driver error strings returned to clients disclose internals (table and query details) useful for probing, and missing nosniff/HSTS on direct API responses weaken the browser posture for anyone hitting the Render origin directly instead of through the relay.
findings.fix: Mount helmet (CSP relaxed only where needed, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors none) in gateway.ts before routes, and replace res.status(500).json({ error: error.message }) with a generic message plus console-level detail via the structured logger.
findings.verify: rg -c "helmet" backend/src/gateway.ts && rg -n "error: error.message" backend/src/server.ts (expect header mount >=1 and message leak count reduced)

findings.title: CI installs with npm install despite lockfiles, uses floating action tags, and has no SCA gate
findings.impact: Builds do not verify the committed dependency graph (install can drift from package-lock.json), third-party actions float on mutable major tags, and no automated vulnerability gate exists, so a compromised or vulnerable release can ship silently.
findings.fix: Switch both workflows to npm ci, pin checkout/setup-node to 40-char commit SHAs, and add an osv-scanner or npm-audit step gated on high with no soft-fail.
findings.verify: grep -c "npm ci" .github/workflows/*.yml && grep -Ec "uses: .*@[0-9a-f]{40}" .github/workflows/vercel-production-check.yml

findings.title: Redacting logger exists but is never wired; security events go through raw console calls
findings.impact: Passcode-shaped values or origins reaching logs are never redacted (paper control), and failed-auth events leave no trace, making brute-force attempts invisible until cost anomalies appear.
findings.fix: Import the structured logger everywhere, replace the 41 console call sites, and add warn-level events with IP+outcome to passcodeAuth denial and cron-secret failures.
findings.verify: rg -n "console\.(log|error|warn)" backend/src | wc -l (expect ~0) && rg -n "logger.warn" backend/src/server.ts (expect >=1 in passcodeAuth)

findings.title: Deployed app ships no security disclosure baseline (SECURITY.md / security.txt)
findings.impact: A researcher who finds the brute-forceable shared-passcode design has no contact channel, increasing the chance of public disclosure rather than a report.
findings.fix: Add SECURITY.md with a contact address and, ideally, serve /.well-known/security.txt from the frontend.
findings.verify: test -f SECURITY.md

findings.title: Bill-pay endpoint pays an arbitrary unpaid bill when the requested bill id does not exist
findings.impact: POST /api/finance/bill/pay with a stale or wrong id marks the newest unpaid bill paid and books an expense for it, silently corrupting finance records instead of returning 404; the same operation behaves differently depending on which of the two backends handles it.
findings.fix: Delete the findFirst fallback in backend/src/server.ts and return 404 like the relay implementation; add a regression test asserting unknown ids return 404 and mutate nothing.
findings.verify: rg -n "paid: false" backend/src/server.ts (expect 0 within /api/finance/bill/pay)

findings.title: Progress-score loop persists nothing: cron finalize_yesterday is a silent no-op while WeeklyReport stays dead
findings.impact: The 04:00 IST cron computes dailyScore from yesterday's tasks then discards it (server.ts:1605-1612, only a console.log) yet returns status:"completed" (server.ts:1615), so operators and CronJobMonitor believe finalization ran. WeeklyReport (schema.prisma:121, migration table exists) has zero code readers/writers; ConceptExplanation is write-only (created server.ts:2008, never served); TopicStatus is touched only by delete cascades (server.ts:2168). Streaks/comeback scoring promised by the job name lands nowhere.
findings.fix: In the 04:00 block, upsert dailyScore onto RoutinePlan (or create the WeeklyReport row aggregating Mon-Sun scores) before returning success; either wire ConceptExplanation/TopicStatus into an explainer history view or drop them from the schema; make the endpoint 509/no-op-explicit if intentionally deferred.
findings.verify: rg -n "weeklyReport.create|weeklyReport.upsert|score:" backend/src returns >=1 persistence call inside the currentHour === 4 block; GET /cron/tick during hour 4 then shows a non-null stored score for yesterday.

findings.title: Same API surface implemented twice (Next relay native handlers vs Express) plus unreachable duplicate finance registrations with stale Supabase messaging
findings.impact: frontend/app/api/backend/[...path]/route.ts:43-709 natively re-implements tracker/routine/subjects/finance handlers that backend/src/server.ts also serves; the relay tries native-first (comment line 742) and falls back to relaying to Express, so two codebases own one contract and will drift independently (already each carries its own copy of bill-pay expense-upsert logic). Inside server.ts itself, DELETE /api/finance/bill/:id, DELETE /api/finance/bill and POST /api/finance/reset are each registered twice (2802+2842, 2816+2853, 2830+2864); Express keeps the first, so the second trio is dead weight that still references raw `(prisma as any).financeBill` and answers "reset successfully in Supabase" — a stale message from the pre-Prisma era. Dead-code remediation cross-ref F-CODE.
findings.fix: Pick one owner per path: keep the Next-native handlers and strip those routes from server.ts (or invert). Delete the second registrations at server.ts:2842-2873 outright and correct the surviving reset message.
findings.verify: rg -n 'app.(delete|post)("/api/finance/(bill|reset)' backend/src/server.ts returns exactly one registration per path; rg -n Supabase backend/src returns 0 hits.

findings.title: Scaffold `any` stub types and dual model-name casts blind compile-time checking of core entities
findings.impact: server.ts:14-18 declares type Journal = any; ProgressRating = any; Subject = any; Task = any — scaffolding for 'prior to running prisma generate', left in place even though the build script always runs prisma generate first. Every task filter callback typed (t: Task) is compile-time unchecked. The same uncertainty leaks as defensive dual-name casts ((prisma as any).task || (prisma as any).Task, .routinePlan || .RoutinePlan, .financeExpense || .FinanceExpense) throughout server.ts and the Next relay, so a schema rename would fail silently at runtime instead of at tsc.
findings.fix: Delete the four stub aliases and import generated types from @prisma/client; settle canonical camelCase delegate names once and remove the || fallback casts (or gate them behind one typed accessor helper).
findings.verify: rg -n "type Journal = any|= any;" backend/src/server.ts returns 0; rg -n "as any\)\.task \|\|" backend/src frontend returns 0; npx tsc --noEmit clean in backend.

findings.title: Zero automated tests across backend, frontend, mobile and worker despite CI and jest tooling being present
findings.impact: No *.test.* or *.spec.* file exists in any workspace; mobile/package.json wires jest-expo (scripts.test, jest preset) yet ships zero test files. Every shipped vertical (auth verify, routine tasks, tracker log upsert, finance bill-pay double-entry, interview session summary, journal encryption) has no integration or permission test, so the 54-file dirty redesign can regress contracts undetected. Whole-suite existence/CI wiring belongs to repo (cross-ref F-REPO); this records the per-feature coverage gap this module owns.

findings.title: No rate limiting on passcode auth or mutations, and the hardening header set is partial
findings.impact: The single passcode gates everything (backend x-passcode middleware server.ts:267-279; web POST /api/auth timing-safe compare), yet zero rate-limit code exists anywhere (rg rate-limit|helmet: 0 hits) on internet-exposed Render/Vercel hosts — unlimited online brute-force against an 8+-char shared secret is possible, and every AI mutation can be hammered through the relay. Headers: x-content-type-options nosniff on relay responses and Referrer-Policy on journal payloads only; no CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy baseline. Secrets themselves stay security's (cross-ref F-SEC); pipeline placement of limits cross-ref F-DEPLOY when CI runs one.
findings.fix: Add express-rate-limit (strict window on /api/auth/verify and POST /api/auth, looser global bucket) and set the five headers via Next config/proxy.ts for web plus helmet-equivalent for Express; exempt /health.
findings.verify: rg -n "rateLimit|helmet|Content-Security-Policy" backend/src frontend returns hits on the auth paths; repeated failed POST /api/auth returns 429 after threshold.

findings.title: Money columns are Float across the finance schema
findings.impact: FinanceExpense.amount (schema.prisma:213), FinanceBill.amount (:237) and FinanceBudget.allowance (:225) are Float. No live payment flow exists (personal ledger, UPI tracking only) so this is not Critical, but rupee-and-paise values summed in JS floats can accumulate cent-level drift against caps and the bill-pay double-entry copy. If the database pass carries the identical root cause, cross-reference F-DB instead of double-billing this fix.
findings.fix: Migrate the three columns to Decimal(12,2) (or integer paise) with one migration; convert at the form boundary only.
findings.verify: rg -n "amount\s+Float|allowance\s+Float" prisma/schema.prisma backend/prisma/schema.prisma returns 0 hits after migration.

findings.impact: sandbox-chat (frontend/app/sandbox-chat/page.tsx) renders MOCK_DRAFTS sample templates ('One focused subject', etc.) but no nav item, Link, or router.push anywhere references it — an orphaned scaffold page reachable only by typed URL. backend/src/debug_logs.ts survives from the prior audit with its console.log lines and compiles into dist even though nothing imports it. Neither exposes data beyond the logged-in user's own (proxy.ts gates the page), but both are dead surface area contradicting the shipped posture. Dead-code specifics cross-ref F-CODE.

findings.title: Prisma schema triplicated across three packages with CLI version skew — drift waiting to happen
findings.impact: Three content-synced copies of schema.prisma exist: prisma/schema.prisma (root, owns migrations), backend/prisma/schema.prisma (backend build + migrate target), frontend/prisma/schema.prisma (frontend `npx prisma generate` target). Today they match except a trailing blank line (git diff --no-index: 1 deletion between root and each other; backend==frontend byte-identical), but nothing enforces sync — commit af6a1bc already moved one copy for Render, proving copies diverge by edit location. Root pins prisma ^5.22.0 while backend pins ^5.10.2, so generators can emit differently-versioned clients from 'the same' schema.
findings.fix: Keep backend/prisma/schema.prisma as the single source (it owns runtime + migrations); make root and frontend thin consumers via a sync script or prisma folder field, and align the three prisma/* versions to ^5.22.0.
findings.verify: After wiring: editing backend/prisma/schema.prisma and running root+frontend builds fails loudly if out of sync (or hash-compare step in CI passes); lockfiles show one resolved prisma version family.

findings.title: A second backend implementation inside the Vercel relay duplicates Express domain logic with divergent semantics
findings.impact: The same operation behaves differently depending on which platform handles it: fixes applied to one copy silently miss the other, and the drift has already shipped a finance-mutation defect (arbitrary bill payment) that the relay copy does not have. Two platforms hold DATABASE_URL and write the same tables with different invariant enforcement.
findings.fix: Choose one writer per table: delete the native tracker/routine/finance handlers from the relay and always forward to Express, or extract shared domain logic into one package consumed by both. Add contract tests asserting identical responses from both surfaces for the same payload.

findings.impact: A bad deploy, accidental reset endpoint call (/api/tracker/reset and /api/finance/reset wipe tables irreversibly), or Supabase free-tier data loss destroys the user's entire history with no recovery; the PRD's durability promise is unmet.
findings.fix: Add a weekly cron job (the existing /cron/tick harness) that exports all tables to JSON and pushes them to Cloudflare R2 or the D1 store, plus document a restore procedure; gate /reset endpoints behind a confirmation token.

findings.impact: Journal entries, OCR text from uploaded images, topics, tags, and conversation history are concatenated into the same channel the model treats as trusted instructions; crafted content can override the mentor's constraints and steer output toward downstream consumers, including the renderer sinks already filed as F-SEC-1.
findings.fix: Pass durable instructions in the system role and move ALL user/retrieved content into user-role messages wrapped in explicit delimiters (<user_entry>...</user_entry>); add an instruction-resistance line and validate that template variables never contain the delimiters.

findings.title: Parsed AI responses enter app state without schema validation outside the interview surface
findings.impact: Malformed or hostile model output shapes propagate into Postgres and back to the browser renderer (the F-SEC-1 execution sink), producing runtime TypeErrors on odd shapes today and a persistent injection channel tomorrow; zod is already a backend dependency but is unused on these paths.
findings.fix: Define one zod schema per AI surface (explainer session/sections/quiz, plan-chat draftTasks/suggestions, general-chat action/layout) with additionalProperties restrictions; validate before persistence and return the structured parse error to the retry loop.

findings.title: AI spend is unbounded: no quota layer and no usage accounting
findings.impact: One leaked passcode converts directly into an open wallet: explainer vision calls and long generations can be invoked at unlimited rate with zero token attribution, and cost anomalies are invisible because usage is never recorded.
findings.fix: Capture response.usage into AiCallLog (promptTokens/completionTokens columns), add a per-day call/token ceiling checked in resolveAiConfiguration before dispatch, and mount the rate limiter from F-SEC-2 in front of AI routes.

findings.impact: The mentor personality edited through settings silently reverts on every Render deploy, and the write path lets any passcode holder mutate the instruction file that every AI surface loads, with no version history.

findings.title: Model responses are consumed without checking finish_reason or truncation
findings.impact: Length-truncated completions enter the JSON repair pipeline as if complete, burning the fallback retry and degrading answer quality; a fresh OpenAI client per request adds connection churn on every mentor interaction.
findings.fix: Branch on choices[0].finish_reason ('length' triggers a continuation or explicit degradation), hoist one OpenAI instance per provider into module scope keyed by credential, and treat refusals explicitly.
findings.verify: rg -n "finish_reason" backend/src/lib/ai/provider.ts (expect >=1)

findings.title: Personal journal and study content is sent to LLM providers unminimized with no data-control configuration
findings.impact: The product documents journals as private enough to encrypt at rest and isolate in D1, then transmits their plaintext (plus name, mood, study notes) to third-party model providers over ordinary API terms; the privacy posture is inconsistent between storage and inference.
findings.fix: Document the inference-privacy boundary in PRD, prefer providers with no-training/no-retention terms (OpenRouter provider routing flags where supported), strip or pseudimize name/history context where the feature tolerates it, and record the tradeoff next to the D1 encryption rationale.

findings.impact: Every regression class this audit found (arbitrary bill payment, retired journal endpoint still called by web clients, drift between two backends) ships silently; auth, money mutations, and AI parsing have no failure-case coverage.

findings.impact: A long-running process accumulates study logs twice, memory creeps toward free-tier caps, and after restart the fallback is empty so reads depend entirely on D1 - inverted fallback semantics.

findings.impact: Currency sums accumulate binary floating-point error (0.1+0.2 class) in exactly the budget-vs-spending comparisons the finance module exists for; the check catalog marks floating-point money a hard-cap defect, calibrated here to High because the flows are display-grade single-user records with no settlement or reconciliation against external money.

findings.impact: Task lookups by planId and date devolve to full scans as history grows, and AiCallLog grows on every AI call with no index for surface/time pruning; negligible today at personal scale, compounding yearly.

findings.fix: Add engines.node >=22 to every package.json plus a .nvmrc, set node-version: 22 in both workflows, and pin Render's NODE_VERSION env to 22.
findings.verify: rg -c node-version: 22 .github/workflows expects 2 and Test-Path .nvmrc expects true

findings.title: Phantom dependencies: backend iron-session unused; root manifest vestigial with version skew
findings.impact: Unused dependencies expand the audit surface, confuse install contexts (which manifest wins depends on invocation directory), and invite wrong-package imports later.
findings.fix: Remove iron-session from backend/package.json; delete the root package.json or give it a real role (workspace scripts) with matching prisma versions.
findings.verify: rg -c iron-session backend/package.json expects 0

findings.title: No stack decision record exists (alternatives, flip points, switching cost)
findings.impact: The bundle works today, but future churn (AI provider changes, Supabase pricing cliffs) will be decided from memory rather than criteria; cheap to fix given the PRD already holds half the content.
findings.fix: Add docs/adr/0001-stack-bundle.md capturing pre-flight answers, one rejected alternative per slot, a numeric ceiling (e.g. single user, <100 req/day), and the re-check trigger (any paid tier or second user).
findings.verify: Test-Path docs/adr/0001-stack-bundle.md

findings.title: Success metrics lack thresholds, deadlines, and named sources
findings.impact: The product's own headline bet (the daily loop is the moat) cannot be verified or refuted because engagement is never operationalized; two of three recorded metrics prove the author can write testable metrics.
findings.fix: Rewrite the success block as three measurable lines (e.g. log completion >=5 days/week measured from StudyLog rows monthly; dashboard TTI <2s on free tier; monthly AI cost <= X via AiCallLog counts) and review them in the cron weekly summary.
findings.verify: rg -c measured PRD.md expects >=2 quantified metrics

findings.title: Requirements are not priority-ranked and NFR thresholds are incomplete
findings.impact: Scope cuts under time pressure happen by intuition rather than by rank; only one of ten NFR dimensions has a number, so regressions against intent are undetectable.
findings.fix: Tag Section 3 modules Must/Should/Could within the existing caps and give durability, privacy, and AI-quality NFRs one threshold each (backup age, journal encryption coverage, JSON parse success rate from AiCallLog).
findings.verify: rg -c Must PRD.md Section 3 expects >=5 ranked items

findings.title: No route-level loading or error boundaries exist in the web app
findings.impact: Any render-time exception blanks the entire route with Next's default crash screen instead of an in-context recovery message, and slow AI-backed navigations (90-second provider timeouts) leave users on stale screens with only per-page spinners as a cue.
findings.fix: Add app/loading.tsx skeletons for dashboard/journal/tracker/explainer and a root app/error.tsx (plus per-route error.tsx where recovery differs) that offers retry and preserves the shell.
findings.verify: Get-ChildItem -Recurse frontend/app -Include loading.tsx,error.tsx -File | Measure-Object expects >=4

findings.title: Destructive reset endpoints wipe data irreversibly with no undo or confirmation artifact
findings.impact: One accidental tap (or one leaked passcode) erases months of finance and study history instantly; combined with the absent backups this is unrecoverable data loss by design.
findings.fix: Require a typed-confirmation field (e.g. confirm:"DELETE") validated server-side, add a 7-day soft-delete flag instead of hard deleteMany, and exclude these routes from batch automation.
findings.verify: rg -n confirm backend/src/server.ts within reset handlers expects >=2

findings.title: Arbitrary Tailwind values bypass the design-token scale
findings.impact: Hardcoded px sizes and raw palette colors drift from the token system that dark mode depends on, producing off-theme patches exactly where AI content renders most often; the project's own AGENTS.md rule declares tokens authoritative.
findings.fix: Add text-[10px]/[11px] steps to the token scale (or map to text-xs) and replace raw red-50/red-700 with danger tokens (--danger exists); enforce with a grep gate for bracket-value classes outside a whitelist.

findings.title: CI triggers only on two stale side branches and executes no tests
findings.impact: Commits to the default branch run zero verification - no typecheck, no build, nothing - so the main line can break while CI sits green on side branches; the verify-audit-fixes workflow's security assertions (no hardcoded passcode, no console.log) never execute on current code.
findings.fix: Add one workflow triggering on push to the default branch plus pull_request that runs frontend typecheck+build, backend tsc, and (once F-CODE-5 lands) the test suite; retire or generalize the stale fix-branch workflow.
findings.verify: rg -n branches .github/workflows expects default-branch trigger present
